newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR WEAKENS IN SHORT MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR WEAKENS IN SHORT MARKET.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar weakened on major currencies in a short early interbank market on Thursday, foreign exchange dealers said.
"We opened at 11.67/68 (against the key U.S. dollar) then all of a sudden there were buyers in the market and the rate has gone down...and the spread has widened," a dealer said.
"We're running short of foreign exchange. The central bank might intervene but if they are happy with where the (Zimbabwe) dollar is going they might not," he added.
At 0745 GMT, the local unit was quoted at 11.6900/7200 on the U.S. dollar from 11.6700/6800 at Wednesday's close.
It lost ground to sterling against which it was indicated at 18.4900/5600 versus 18.3860/4080 and also to a strong overseas German mark on which it was quoted at 6.3500/3600 from 6.3200/3290.
Against the rand of South Africa, Zimbabwe's biggest trading partner in Africa, it firmed marginally to 2.5000/5100 compared to 2.5020/5050.
